new_statements.quote: From rather early in this exploration of the full/reduced contrast it seemed that such a contrast could have arisen from differences of accentual patterns at an earlier stage even though an accentual difference is not evident in the contemporary Land Dayak languages. They consistently accent the final syllable of the stem; this is especially evident in utterance-final position.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (accent) is fixed on the final syllable of the stem in all contemporary Land Dayak languages, the Bakati' cluster (Rara, Sara/Riok, Kendayan, Bekati') included; Sudarsono's Bakatik description (Riuk+Sara+Lara cluster) independently states that word stress 'generally falls on the word-final syllable' and is predictable, hence not phonemic.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned for Land Dayak/Bakati'; Sudarsono 2013 snippet describes Bakatik rhythm as syllable-based with word stress integrated into the intonation system, no secondary stress mentioned.
new_statements.exceptions: Rensch: 'especially evident in utterance-final position' (implies weaker prominence elsewhere); for Bidayuh the ultima carries stress 'at least in citation forms' and a clitic takes the word stress (fn.79 p.94). Sudarsono 2013: 'generally' word-final. No Sara-specific exceptions recorded anywhere.
new_statements.domain_note: Family-level generalization over Land Dayak stems, made by an author whose Proto Bakati' chapter (pp.211-225) uses Sara/Riok wordlist data from Bryant 1990; the Bidayuh-specific statement is explicitly about citation forms. Sudarsono 2013's Bakatik statement is language-level (Riuk/Sara/Lara cluster) but snippet-only, no page.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is a family-level claim about 'the contemporary Land Dayak languages' (Bidayuh + Bakati' + Southern Land Dayak) by an author whose Proto Bakati' chapter uses Sara/Riok data from Bryant 1990; it is not a Sara-specific description. The corroborating Sudarsono 2013 statement is for 'Bakatik' = Riuk + Sara + Lara(=Rara) dialects (Sudarsono 2002:10), which Grambank maps to beka1241 'Riuk Bekati'' rather than sara1329; Glottolog lists 'Riok' as an alternate name of sara1329, so Sudarsono's Bakatik overlaps sara1329 and rara1235 but the dialect base of his phonology is unknown. No opened source describes Sara Bakati' alone.

Part II 4.1.2 p.47 (PDF p.64): Bidayuh ultima 'receives the peak of word stress--at least in citation forms'. Sara/Riok enters only as comparative wordlist data from Bryant (Part III sec. 3 'Proto Bakati'' pp.211-225, fn.48-49 p.212); no Sara/Riok-specific stress remark and no stress marks on Sara/Riok forms.
